rules.description: keep the most recent 10 release-* images (immediate rollback window)
expire non-official sha-* candidates after 30 days
expire the mutable main-latest convenience tag after 30 days
expire mutable branch-* convenience tags after 30 days
expire untagged images after a 14-day grace period

notes: Pass 3, subphase 3.8 desired ECR lifecycle policy, identical for every backend repository. Rule order is load-bearing: ECR evaluates every rule and an image is expired by exactly one or zero rules; an image matching a higher-priority rule's tagging requirements can never be expired by a lower-priority rule (first-match-wins). Rule 1 therefore has the HIGHEST priority so a retained multi-tag release image (sha-* + release-*) inside the newest 10 is claimed by the keep-10 rule and the candidate rules never apply to it. ECR requires every tagged rule to carry an explicit tagPrefixList, so the candidate families (sha-*, main-latest, branch-*) MUST be enumerated — a generic negative/exclusion filter ('expire everything except releases') is not expressible and is never used; any tag outside the declared families is retained (fail-safe). Every tagged rule selects EXACTLY ONE tag prefix: AWS documents that a multi-entry tagPrefixList/tagPatternList selects only images carrying ALL the listed tags ('only the images with all specified tags are selected'), so a merged ['main-latest', 'branch-'] rule would silently select nothing — each family gets its own single-prefix rule (2, 3, 4), which is unambiguous under ECR's documented semantics, and the validator rejects multi-entry prefix lists (POLICY_TAGPREFIX_MULTI). ECR lifecycle evaluation is delayed (a policy change is applied by ECR's periodic evaluator, up to 24 hours); images referenced by manifest lists or OCI referrers are not selected. Preview with release/bin/preview-retention-policy.sh before any apply; apply only via release/bin/apply-retention-policy.sh (refused offline; the consolidated Pass 3 live pass sets ONLINESHOP_RETENTION_LIVE_APPLY=1) with immediate get-lifecycle-policy read-back.
